THE ESSENTIALS

What is a Director Payroll?

Even as the founder and sole director of your UK Limited Company, any money you take out for personal use must be officially categorized. You cannot simply transfer company funds into your personal account.

Setting up a PAYE (Pay As You Earn) scheme allows you to pay yourself a formal salary. It provides legally recognized proof of income, reduces your company's Corporation Tax burden, and ensures total compliance with HMRC's strict extraction rules.

Why Run a Payroll?

  • Tax Efficiency: A small salary is a deductible business expense, lowering Corporation Tax.
  • Proof of Income: Formal payslips are vital for mortgages, visas, and banking.
  • Legal Extraction: Avoid harsh tax penalties from illegal "Director's Loans."
THE RISK

The Danger of Unreported Income

Withdrawing funds without the proper HMRC mechanisms in place will result in severe financial consequences.

The Section 455 Tax Trap

If you take money out without declaring it as salary or dividends, HMRC classifies it as a Director's Loan. If unpaid within 9 months of your year-end, a heavy 33.75% tax penalty is applied to the balance.

Missed RTI Penalties

If you are registered for PAYE but fail to submit your Real Time Information (RTI) reports to HMRC on or before payday, you will incur automatic monthly fines starting at £100.

Higher Corporation Tax

By only extracting funds via dividends (which are drawn from post-tax profits), you miss out on the Corporation Tax deduction that a structured director's salary provides.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

PAYE (Pay As You Earn) is HMRC's system to collect Income Tax and National Insurance from employment. Even as a sole director of your own UK Limited Company, you are technically an employee. Running a payroll allows you to pay yourself a formal, legal salary.

Paying yourself a small, tax-efficient salary (up to the National Insurance threshold) counts as a deductible business expense, reducing your company's Corporation Tax. It also gives you a qualifying year towards a UK State Pension (if eligible) without actually paying any Income Tax or National Insurance.

No. Non-resident directors can still be paid a salary for their duties managing a UK company. However, the tax implications (whether you pay tax in the UK or your home country) depend on your residency status and dual taxation treaties. We advise on the most compliant approach.

Unreported transfers are classified as a 'Director's Loan' by HMRC. If not repaid, they are subject to a hefty tax charge (currently 33.75%). All money extracted for personal use must be officially declared as salary (via PAYE) or dividends (via company resolutions).

RTI is HMRC's mandatory reporting system. It requires employers to report payroll information, including salaries, taxes, and deductions, to HMRC on or before the day employees are paid. Our service handles these RTI submissions automatically every month.

We can set up an annual payroll scheme if you prefer to take your salary in one lump sum at the end of the tax year. However, monthly payroll is generally recommended to provide a steady, documented income stream, which helps with personal finance applications.

The £49/month fee is specifically for a single-director payroll setup. If you hire additional staff (UK or international), we can scale your payroll scheme to include them for a small additional fee per employee.

Yes. Every month you will receive a formal, HMRC-compliant digital payslip detailing your gross pay, deductions (if any), and net pay. These payslips are vital proof of income for visas, mortgages, or personal banking.

A P60 is a certificate issued at the end of the tax year (April) summarizing your total pay and deductions for that year. It is a critical document for proving your annual income. Generation of your P60 is included in our service.

Missing an RTI submission deadline to HMRC results in automatic late filing penalties, which accumulate quickly. By letting us manage your payroll, you ensure submissions are made strictly on time, avoiding all fines.

Registering a new PAYE scheme with HMRC typically takes 1 to 2 weeks. Once you receive your Employer PAYE Reference and Accounts Office Reference, we can immediately begin processing your monthly payroll.
